root_cause.text: The switch statement in `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` was missing cases for masked atomic opcodes (`IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD` and `IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP`), causing masked atomic completions to fall through to the default branch, where `rm` is returned as NULL while `send->s_op` remains set, leading to a NULL pointer dereference in `rds_ib_send_cqe_handler()` when it accesses `rm->m_final_op`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description explicitly states: "the completion-side switch in `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` only handles the non-masked opcodes, so a masked atomic completion falls through to default and returns rm == NULL while send->s_op is left set." The patch diff adds the two masked atomic opcodes to the same case as the non-masked atomic opcodes, confirming the missing cases were the root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the function `rds_ib_send_unmap_op()` with a switch statement that handles IB_WR_SEND, IB_WR_RDMA_WRITE/READ, IB_WR_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD, and IB_WR_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP, but does not include cases for masked atomic opcodes (IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_FETCH_AND_ADD and IB_WR_MASKED_ATOMIC_CMP_AND_SWP). This causes masked atomic completions to fall through to the default branch (line: `printk(KERN_NOTICE "RDS/IB: %s: unexpected opcode 0x%x in WR!\n", __func__, send->s_wr.opcode);`) and return NULL, while `send->s_op` remains set. Later in `rds_ib_send_cq_comp_handler`, the code uses `rm` (which is NULL) in `&rm->m_final_op` (line: `if (&send->s_op == &rm->m_final_op)`), leading to a NULL pointer dereference. The fix (adding the missing masked atomic cases) is absent in this commit.
